page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-1 is an ARM-based general-purpose server instance. It features 1 dedicated vCPU powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz, paired with 4.0 GB of system memory. The CPU architecture is arm64, utilizing a single physical core and a single thread per core. It includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the single-core performance of the Neoverse-N1 processor is moderate, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1783.48 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1018.0, placing it in the average to weak categories. However, due to its single-core limitation, multi-core benchmarks are low, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1017.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 766.57. Memory bandwidth is also limited, measuring 11.99 GB/sec for large block reads and 7.95 GB/sec for large block writes. Redis SET operations reach 1.27 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is recorded at 1.38 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance serves as a low-cost entry point into ARM-based cloud computing, offering dedicated CPU resources without the overhead of larger instances. The lack of local storage and low memory bandwidth represent clear tradeoffs for resource-intensive applications. The t2a-standard-1 is best utilized for lightweight workloads such as ARM64 software compilation testing, basic web serving, microservices, and simple utility scripts that do not require high memory throughput or multi-threaded processing.
